ideas.title: Football with the sun
ideas.idea: The sun falls out of the sky into the meadow, and my friends do the only thing they know to do with a round thing: they kick it. The island goes dark blue; the only light is the ball. Every kick whips every shadow on the island round at once: trees, the cottage, the friends' own long shadows swinging like clock hands as the sun rolls between their feet. Kick it into the pond and the water glows from inside; when it rolls into the sea the island goes black until someone fishes it out. The player can jump in and dribble the sun too.
ideas.form: the island's sun and sky light handed to the game's ball: a playable rule (the ball is the light, the sky dims while it is down) for the friends and the player; a path traced film low in the meadow, shadows sweeping on every kick

ideas.title: Lit from below
ideas.idea: The sun sinks into the sea and keeps shining from under the water. The whole island is lit upside down: light comes up through the waves, rippling caustics crawl over the undersides of the tree crowns, the cottage eaves and the friends' chins, like faces over a torch, and the sky above is black.
ideas.form: the sun moved under a glass sea so all light passes through moving water; a traced film drifting under the trees at the shore

ideas.title: A puddle of sky came down
ideas.idea: A sheet of liquid mirror hangs ten metres over the meadow and stays: the island upside down overhead, my friends meeting themselves on the ceiling. They climb the tallest tree to touch it, and drops of sky drip off, fall, and roll through the grass as silver beads that merge into little mirror puddles.
ideas.form: a low conductor sheet over the meadow plus falling mirror drops that roll and merge on the terrain; a traced film from below
